candidates.name: Practice Guide 40 supplement 1: basis of HM Land Registry plans
verified_facts: HM Land Registry states that Ordnance Survey mapping shows topographical features existing at the time of survey.
The mapping detail is multi-purpose and is not intended to represent property boundaries.
semantic_limits: A mapped topographic feature is not by itself the legal boundary and provides no parcel-specific elevation or vertical-accuracy evidence.

candidates.name: Practice Guide 40 supplement 2: preparing plans
verified_facts: Plans lodged with an application must allow the land to be clearly identified on the Ordnance Survey map.
Insufficient plans can lead to rejection, requisition or cancellation.
semantic_limits: Registration identifiability and plan acceptability do not establish centimetre-level geometry or terrain-height accuracy.
